Package com.bilt.pos.session

Class SettlementFlow

java.lang.Object
com.bilt.pos.session.SettlementFlow
public final class SettlementFlow extends Object
The settlement orchestration chain returned by CheckoutSession.settle().

Registering handlers sends nothing. With the default settlement option, the sequence is refund allocations (including external register-managed refunds), rebate redemption, point redemption, stored value tender, card charge, stored value line fulfillment, and award. With net settlement, only the signed basket difference is charged or refunded. The sequence runs when execute() (asynchronously, on the session's operation thread), executeSync() (blocking), get(), or getOrNull() is invoked. Each step handler receives that step's result and returns the updated total for the next step (letting the register recompute tax on discounted amounts).


 session.settle()
     .onRebatesRedeemed(rebates -> rebates.getSuggestedTotal())
     .onPointsRedeemed(points -> points.getSuggestedTotal())
     .onSuccess(result -> register.printReceipt(result.getMerchantReceipt()))
     .onError(error -> SettlementRecovery.abort())
     .execute();

With execute(), every handler — the step handlers, onSuccess, onError, and onComplete — is delivered through the callback executor (the session builder's callbackExecutor, or the per-flow callbackOn(Executor) override), and the settlement thread waits for each answer: the handlers are part of the settlement negotiation, so their return values steer the sequence exactly as if they ran inline — they just physically run on the integrator's thread. Keep them quick (settlement is paused while they run), and never block a callback thread on this flow's get() — the flow would be waiting on that thread's handler while it waits on the flow. Without a callback executor, handlers run directly on the thread executing the sequence.

If a charge-side step fails after refund allocations, onError is called before recovery begins. Its SettlementRecovery retries only the failed step, skips an optional step, records an external final tender, aborts and unwinds, or abandons the partial flow to the register. Earlier successful steps remain committed unless the register returns SettlementRecovery.abort(). Refund allocation failures are different: they are not retried in the same run, and committed refund allocations are not unwound. Retry by calling settle() again with the same committed allocation prefix. The default charge-side policy (no handler) is abort().

Movement callbacks are immediate observations, not the authoritative final ledger. An abort may reverse charge-side movements, and retrying, skipping, or replacing a partially committed failed step first reverses only that step's partial movements. Those reversals do not emit compensating movement callbacks. Refund allocation movements are durable because settlement never unwinds them. Treat SettlementResult.getMovements() from a successful result as the final movement ledger.

      public SettlementFlow onMovement(Consumer<SettlementMovement> handler)
      Called after any externally visible money or loyalty movement commits.

      Charge-side movement callbacks are provisional: an abort can unwind them, and retrying, skipping, or replacing a partially committed failed step can reverse that step's movements without emitting a compensating callback. Earlier successful steps remain committed. Refund allocation movements are not unwound. Use SettlementResult.getMovements() from the successful result as the authoritative final ledger.

    • onError

      public SettlementFlow onError(Function<SettlementFailure,SettlementRecovery> handler)
      Called before any charge-side recovery or unwind begins. The returned SettlementRecovery retries or skips the failed step, records an external tender, aborts with unwind, or abandons recovery to the register. An indeterminate terminal request is checked with TransactionStatus before retry, skip, external replacement, or abort; abandon performs no such I/O. For refund allocation failures, the handler is a terminal failure notification: the returned recovery decision is ignored, committed refund allocations stay recorded, and the register retries with the same committed allocation prefix. Default charge-side policy: abort().

    • onAbandoned

      public SettlementFlow onAbandoned(Consumer<AbandonedSettlementRecord> handler)
      Called when SettlementRecovery.abandon() transfers recovery ownership.

    • onComplete

      public SettlementFlow onComplete(Runnable handler)
      Registers a hook that runs exactly once after settlement completes, on every path — success, failure, unexpected exception, or rejection because the session ended before settlement could run. The place for cleanup that must not leak. A throwing hook is logged, never propagated.

    • execute

      public final void execute()
      Runs the flow asynchronously on the session's operation thread — handlers included, see the class docs — and returns immediately. When the session has already ended and its executor rejects the submission, the flow fails with SessionErrorCode.INVALID_STATE through onError and onComplete.
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the flow has already run

    • executeSync

      public final void executeSync()
      Runs the flow blocking — the operation takes its turn on the session's operation thread (queueing behind anything in flight, so a sync call never races an asynchronous one) while the caller waits; handlers dispatch on the calling thread.
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the flow has already run

    • get

      public final SettlementResult get()
      Runs the flow if it has not run yet and returns the result. Waits for an in-flight execute() to settle first.
      Throws:
      SessionException - if the flow failed
